alias: Self Justice / BlackBar Press — independent civic education
primary_question: When a TV program quotes a president, what independently verifiable government, university, and securities records support each distinct claim?

sources.title: 60 Minutes — Trump November 8, 2026 interview transcript
sources.claim: A CBS transcript documents President Trump's 2026 post-midterm interview; publication is evidence that words were reported, not legal authentication of their accuracy or other allegations.

sources.title: Meet the Attorney General — Todd Blanche
sources.claim: Todd Blanche serves as Attorney General in 2026 and previously represented Trump in criminal cases.

sources.title: DOJ disclosures — Epstein files and redaction notices
sources.claim: DOJ supplies public disclosure records and describes efforts to protect victims' identities; the index cannot prove every decision was correct.

sources.title: Attorney General William Barr statement on Epstein's death
sources.claim: Barr's 2019 statement sought FBI and DOJ Inspector General investigations; it does not prove a claimed conspiracy.

sources.title: DOJ OIG report on detention and supervision
sources.claim: OIG found serious failures in Bureau of Prisons custody, care and supervision, which must be distinguished from unrelated financial allegations.

sources.title: MIT releases independent fact-finding on Epstein ties
sources.claim: MIT reported 10 Epstein donations totaling $850,000 between 2002 and 2017 and acknowledged serious institutional errors of judgment.

sources.title: American Bitcoin 2026 Q3 SEC exhibit
sources.claim: American Bitcoin filed a 2026 quarterly company release. Eric Trump is described as co-founder and chief strategy officer; a company statement is not proof of ties to Epstein or MIT.

questions.text: Does a Sunday CBS transcript independently prove everything said on television?
questions.answer: No. It records what CBS reports; validate material claims with independent evidence.

questions.text: Can we identify who holds the Attorney General's office?
questions.answer: Yes, DOJ lists Todd Blanche as Attorney General as of October 2026.

questions.text: Does a 2019 Barr statement establish which investigations began?
questions.answer: The statement establishes what Barr announced; separate reports establish subsequent investigative findings.

questions.text: Did MIT publicly account for specific Epstein donations?
questions.answer: Yes. MIT's commissioned review identified ten gifts totaling $850,000.

questions.text: Does an SEC filing for American Bitcoin prove cooperation with Epstein, MIT or DOJ?
questions.answer: No. Separate specific transactional or communications evidence would be necessary.

questions.text: Does a redaction automatically prove corruption or censorship?
questions.answer: No. Determine the legal basis, exact redacted record, review authority and any lawful appeal or challenge process.

questions.text: Does this lesson issue a court judgment or close a real case?
questions.answer: No; this is a research lesson only.

readme: The sources are independently grounded URLs. No third-party source was copied into the classroom. A functioning lesson doesn't establish primary-source bytes, permissions, payments, or guilt.
